patch_description: The current algorithm sends every partition of the data along the exact same shortest path (computed once per dst), so all partitions redundantly traverse the same links, driving up cost and congestion. A better strategy: for each destination, compute multiple edge-disjoint low-cost paths (using short path enumeration with a cost cap) and assign different partitions to different paths. This spreads load across networks/links, avoids redundant transfers over the same expensive edges, and exploits multi-network topologies. Additionally, paths should be sorted by cost so the cheapest paths carry partitions first.
